page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8v-8x.16xlarge is a GPU-accelerated instance within the compute-optimized family, running on the KVM hypervisor. Compute is provided by 64 dedicated vCPUs driven by Intel Xeon 8469C processors with an x86_64 architecture operating at a base frequency of 2.6 GHz. System host memory is provisioned at 768 GB, which supplies a dense ratio of 12 GB of RAM per vCPU. Computational acceleration is delivered via 8 dedicated GPUs offering a combined total of 768 GB of GPU memory.

The server contains no integrated local storage, requiring persistent workloads to rely entirely on external network-attached block storage or object storage solutions. Network connectivity is rated at a baseline throughput of 32 Gbps, facilitating rapid inter-node synchronization and external data transfers. The instance does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses by default. In terms of cost efficiency, the configuration consolidates substantial GPU density and high memory capacity within a single virtual server, eliminating underutilized local NVMe drives while maximizing resource availability for GPU-bound pipelines.

This instance configuration is targeted at heavy computational tasks requiring large memory capacities across both host and accelerator domains. Workload profiles that fit this architecture include large-scale deep learning model training, distributed AI inference, complex computer vision pipelines, high-performance computing (HPC) simulations, and memory-intensive GPU data processing.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn8v-8x.16xlarge is a high-density GPU server built on the KVM hypervisor for intensive parallel computing. It is powered by 64 dedicated vCPUs from an Intel Xeon 8469C processor running at 2.6 GHz, coupled with 768 GB of system memory at 12 GB per core. The acceleration layer features 8 GPUs providing an aggregate 768 GB of GPU VRAM. The instance does not feature onboard local storage and relies on external storage volumes, while delivering 32 Gbps of baseline network bandwidth without included public IPv4 addresses. With high accelerator memory density and substantial host memory, the server is structured for distributed deep learning training, large language model inference, parallel scientific simulation workloads, and accelerated big data analytics.
